title: To Doña Justa Sánchez and Don Diego de Tovar
text:
Justa in name, sinful in deeds,

        saint of Cupid's calendar,

        whose miracles her husband has now

        canonized with patience.


        She absolves faults, weeps penances

        for the one who is cousin and perhaps husband at last,

        free cloak trimmed all around,

        which one man pays for and another deflowers.


        What will the widow's crown say,

        seeing that Don Jackass has renewed

        the horn on this unholy Saturday?


        It will say he is a cuckold of bad ending,

        and that he forgets the honor of the regiment,

        and we will say as much.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Golden Age sexual satire, wordplay on Justa, and deliberately coarse cuckold insult.

title: To a Most Beautiful Lady Who Was Burned in a House Fire
text:
Against living snow, delicate and pure,

        treacherous fire showed its enmity;

        no doubt it was jealous of this snow,

        because her whiteness also burned.


        Now Troy's ill-fated disaster

        is a light rigor of the ravenous flame,

        if there it dares against a beautiful city,

        while here it consumes a world of beauty.


        Your embers, O sacrilegious element,

        would have made Clori a wandering Phoenix,

        reborn proud in common pity;


        but how certain it is that with your breath

        you would not have overcome such divine matter

        had human misery not helped you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the conceit of white beauty as living snow burned by jealous fire.

title: To the Omens of Judgment Day
text:
Oh how much one says in one's favor by keeping silent!


Oh how much one says in one's favor by keeping silent!

because to love, to suffer

        is a certain sign,

and silence the purest sacrifice,

and where

        love always finds merit.


To die in one's passion without declaring it

is the true

        office of one who loves,

for a silent weeping as exercise

gives more reason for itself,

        not daring to give it.


Whoever is silent while loving dies loving alone,

for the one who manages

        to speak himself is no care;

one says less and loves more when one loves most.


Because if my silence has not spoken to you,

I do not know how to tell you more than this: if

        I should die,

what I have kept silent has told you enough.
editorial_note: The translation preserves this expanded variant's repeated opening and the silent-love conceit.

title: Silence, in Your Sepulcher I Deposit
text:
Silence, in your sepulcher I deposit

        hoarse voice, blind pen, and sorrowful hand,

        so that my pain may not sing in vain,

        given to the wind and written in sand.


        Tomb and death of oblivion I seek,

        though gray more with warnings than with years,

        where today I yield more than to reason,

        and to time I will give all I take from myself.


        I will limit desires and hopes,

        and in the sphere of a clear disillusion

        I will set brief margins to my life,


        so that I may not be overcome by the snares

        of one who tries to procure my harm

        and occasioned so provident a flight.
editorial_note: The translation keeps silence as tomb, restraint, and protective retreat from snares.

title: I Try Again a Second Time, Fortune
text:
I try again a second time, Fortune,

        the effects of your wrath, aggrieved

        by sad experiences, having observed

        the varied movements of the moon.


        I will dismiss hopes one by one,

        if they went badly, their warnings well achieved,

        when, among deceits already disillusioned,

        ambitious longing no longer troubles me.


        For me, unreasonings are reason;

        in mute suffering I sometimes read

        reports I gave to time of my harm.


        I will silence complaints, I will drink passions,

        so that a second time my desire

        may not step on the threshold of disillusion.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Fortune, disillusion, and mute suffering as a disciplined second trial.
